text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Moslem co-chairman of the Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdjic, met two senior International Civilian Aviation Organisation (ICAO) officials following announced opening of four air corridors over Bosnia beginning on Thursday.

- The International Police Task Force (IPTF) and NATO-led Stabilisation Force will develop a new policy for local police traffic control in an effort to prevent illegal checkpoints between Bosnia's Serb and Moslem-Croat entities, said IPTF spokesman.

- The chief of Mostar's regional office of the High representative, Martin Garrod, condemned the harrassment of two journalists in western Mostar. Local police arrested one Austrian journalist as he was trying to film an Orthodox Christian church near Mostar and beat up an editor of the Moslem national magazine Ljiljan.
- Bosnian Serb republic's National Assembly convenes at ski resort of Jahorina, outside Sarajevo. Deputies will discuss the economic policy of the Serb entity in 1997.

- "Without radical economic reforms, Bosnia and Herzegovina will not recover, irrespectively of how many billions of dollars or German marks is contributed by the international community," says High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt, at opening of a business fair in Tuzla. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
